title: What the referee says on the stand
summary: The short words of the stand: the call, loading and open guns, “one”, “zero” and “No Bird”, and the shooter’s formal word for a protest.

body.html: A stand has its own short language. When ready, the shooter gives the call, usually “Pull!” or “Ready!”. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the referee passes the call to the trapper with a sound signal. The target must leave within 3 seconds of that signal; a later target is a No Bird. In Compak® Sporting a manual release must also come within 3 seconds of the call. A voice-activated release (sonopull: a microphone that launches the target when it hears your call) has a fixed delay of half a second.
“Pull!”, the referee's sound signal to the trapper, the clock, and “No Bird” for a target that comes too late.
body.heading: Watch the call and the release

body.html: Before anyone shoots, the referee decides when guns may be loaded and closed. The rules allow loading only on the stand, with the gun pointing down the range, once the referee has said shooting may start. While targets are being shown (presentation), and whenever shooting stops, guns are open and empty. They are closed again only when the referee allows it. In Compak® Sporting the referee starts the round with “Start” or “Competition”.

After each target there are only three results in the rulebook: “one” (hit), “zero” (lost) and “No Bird” (the target does not count and is thrown again). On the ground you will also hear “dead” or “good” for a hit and “lost” for a miss; some referees say nothing after a hit. In Compak® Sporting the referee announces each zero aloud or with a sound signal, so a shooter who disagrees can protest at once.

The shooter has a formal word too. To disagree with a decision, raise a hand at once, on the stand, and say “Protest!” or “Appeal!” (Chapter 9 · How to protest on the stand, Chapter 19 · How to protest a referee's call). More phrases a shooter needs: Phrases a shooter needs on the stand.

notes.html: Keep these calls short and the same each time. Agree with your shooter before the round which words you will use. Add nothing of your own between the call and the shot.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.meaning: The referee allows shooting to start: put cartridges in now, gun pointing down the range.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.meaning: That target does not count; do not shoot at it. It will be thrown again.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.meaning: The referee scored the target as a miss (zero).

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Guns open, please — we’re showing the targets.
phrases.meaning: Everyone opens and unloads; the referee will throw the targets for viewing.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.meaning: Compak® Sporting: viewing is over, the round counts from now.

key_points.html: The shooter calls “Pull!” or “Ready!”; the target must come within 3 seconds
Load only on the stand and only when the referee allows it; guns open during viewing and stops
Rule words: one = hit, zero = lost, No Bird = thrown again
Compak® Sporting: each zero is announced aloud or by a sound signal

quiz.q: In Sporting™ the target leaves five seconds after the referee’s signal. What is the referee’s decision?

options.text: Zero, because the shooter called too early
A warning for the trapper only

quiz.explain: A target must leave within three seconds of the referee’s signal; a target released later is a No Bird and is thrown again.

quiz.q: In competition, when may a shooter load the gun?

options.text: While walking to the next stand
On the stand, after the referee allows it
As soon as the coach says so

quiz.explain: Loading is allowed only on the stand, gun pointing down the range, and only once the referee has said shooting may start.

quiz.q: Which words start a formal protest on the stand?
quiz.explain: Both rulebooks name “protest” or “appeal” with a raised hand, at once; “No Bird” is the referee’s word.
